speaker: M. L. Kontsevich
title: Formal uniformization of curves and the Virasoro action
summary: The mathematical contribution headed Kontsevich occupies P001258: a curve with a marked point and formal coordinate is acted on by Laurent vector fields, and the Virasoro extension lifts the action to determinant lines. P001257 is a continuation of Beilinson, not part of this contribution. The catalogue date is retained, although the heading visibly reads \(24/\mathrm{II}\text{-}85\); neighboring headings consistently read 1986. Consequently the record cannot establish priority relative to the paper received in December 1986.

speaker: A. Yu. Morozov
title: Bosonic string measure, determinants, and the conformal anomaly
summary: The actual talk begins on P001259 and ends on P001261 before Beilinson. It reduces the critical bosonic-string functional integral formally to a moduli integral and explains the determinants, zero modes, and holomorphic factorization underlying that reduction. Gelfand asks about multiplicativity of regularized determinants. The heading reads \(24.2.86\); the catalogue date is preserved with this disagreement recorded.

speaker: A. A. Beilinson
title: Mixed Hodge structures, real splitting, and Green-function periods
summary: The contribution starts on P001262 and ends at the beginning of P001265. It presents mixed Hodge structures in filtration and split forms, then interprets an extension attached to a punctured curve with two relative marked points through Green functions. The heading reads \(3/\mathrm{III}\text{-}86\), a year earlier than the retained catalogue date.

speaker: A. Yu. Morozov
title: String amplitudes, Green functions, and the superstring measure
summary: The continuation headed Morozov starts midway through P001265 and runs through P001267. It connects the string description to gauge fields, discusses explicit bosonic measures and theta functions, and asks how to obtain the superstring measure by eliminating odd variables. The catalogue range includes neighboring contributions; the items below use the actual headings. The manuscript belongs to the \(3/\mathrm{III}\text{-}86\) session.

speaker: A. Yu. Morozov
title: Compactification, lattice theta series, and heterotic gauge symmetry
summary: The contribution begins on P001268 and continues through P001273. It combines gauge fields, the string oscillator spectrum, compactification on a sixteen-dimensional torus, modular lattice sums, and root vertex operators. Several formulas mix ordinary bosonic compactification with the chiral heterotic construction. The manuscript date is \(10/\mathrm{III}\text{-}86\), whereas the catalogue says 1987.

speaker: D. B. Fuchs
title: Topology of real subspace arrangements and complexifiability
summary: The contribution starts on P001274 and ends on P001276. Fuchs explains the Goresky--MacPherson arrangement theorem through order complexes and stratified Morse theory, including a small example and the special case of \(k\)-arrangements. Gelfand asks about realization, common complex structures, and useful cohomology bases. The manuscript date is \(24.\mathrm{III}.86\), not the catalogue year 1987.

speaker: A. N. Varchenko
title: Asymptotic mixed Hodge structures and singularity spectra
summary: The actual contribution is P001277--P001280. It relates mixed Hodge structures to powers and logarithms in singular integrals, develops the Milnor-fibre setting, and describes the asymptotic filtration and semicontinuity of spectra. Gelfand asks for several functions and for pairs of quadrics. These are separated from the established one-function isolated-singularity theorem.

speaker: I. V. Cherednik
title: RTT algebras, finite-level Yangians, and PBW questions
summary: Cherednik starts on P001281 and finishes near the top of P001282. The rational RTT equation defines a homogeneous version of a truncated Yangian, with a finite-level PBW claim and a level-one enveloping-algebra example. Gelfand asks for a broader quadratic-algebra criterion. Kogan begins later on P001282. The manuscript heading reads \(7/\mathrm{IV}\text{-}86\).

speaker: Yan I. Kogan
title: Covariant bosonic string states, constraints, and string fields
summary: The talk begins midway through P001282 and continues through P001286. It derives the oscillator and Virasoro description, explains the mass tower and physical-state constraints, and moves toward gauge symmetry and interacting string fields. Several sign, mode-index, and level labels are faithfully wrong in the notebook and are emended explicitly. The shared heading reads April 1986.

speaker: I. V. Cherednik
title: Quantum determinants, centers, and fusion
summary: The actual talk occupies P001287--P001289. It repeats the finite-level RTT construction, defines its determinant by antisymmetrization, states the polynomial-center theorem, and uses tensor products and Young diagrams to build representations. Matrix size \(N\) and level \(n\) are repeatedly interchanged in the notebook. The date visibly reads 28 April 1986.

speaker: G. I. Olshanskii
title: A strong-limit enveloping algebra and its Yangian factor
summary: The talk occupies P001290 and the beginning of P001291. It defines an enlargement of the enveloping algebra through bounded-degree, tail-invariant sequences acting on tensor representations, then identifies its central factor and Yangian factor. The exact 1987 Doklady note was presented by Gelfand on 5 May 1986, matching the manuscript heading and independently corroborating the date discrepancy.

speaker: I. V. Cherednik
title: Highest weights and quantum characteristic polynomials
summary: The continuation starts midway through P001291 and runs to the end of P001292. It evaluates the quantum determinant in a highest-weight representation and compares it with ordinary determinants, including a two-dimensional antisymmetrizer calculation. The later year heading and September material on the catalogue range are separate records.

This catalogue record is a year heading, not a separate mathematical talk. The preceding page ends the May quantum-determinant discussion, while P001293 begins the explicitly dated 1 September 1986 session. The overlapping catalogue range does not transfer either contribution to this heading.

speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: Matroids, Coxeter groups, and quadratic duality
summary: The actual contribution begins on P001293. Gelfand discusses work with Serganova on matroids and torus strata, explains the Coxeter-group extension, and then presents quadratic algebras in connection with Beilinson and Ginzburg. The agenda also names Cherednik, but it contains no separate Gelfand--Tsetlin result on these pages. Several elementary examples retain useful manuscript errors: intersection-preserving closure, two-generator finiteness, and the distinction between the two groups of order 120.

speaker: V. L. Ginzburg
title: Complete symmetric varieties and polynomial quotients of affine Hecke algebras
summary: Ginzburg presents the De Concini--Procesi compactification of symmetric varieties, then a finite and affine Hecke-algebra construction. The top of P001298 records a problem attributed explicitly to Cherednik: replace the evaluation of the last lattice generator by a polynomial relation. Ovsienko and Kazakov start separate contributions lower on that page and are indexed with their own records. The catalogue initial is preserved although the mathematical attribution to the speaker known as Victor Ginzburg is conventional.

speaker: V. Yu. Ovsienko
title: KdV and super-KdV as Euler equations
summary: The mathematical report occupies only the middle of P001298, between Ginzburg\textquotesingle s Hecke-algebra discussion and Kazakov\textquotesingle s random surfaces. It identifies KdV and its supersymmetric extensions with Euler equations for Virasoro-type groups; the catalogue\textquotesingle s wide page range does not transfer adjacent talks to Ovsienko.

speaker: V. A. Kazakov
title: Planar maps, matrix integrals, and two-dimensional gravity
summary: The catalogue range overlaps Ginzburg and Ovsienko. Kazakov actually begins in the lower part of P001298 and continues through P001302: triangulated spheres, the cubic Hermitian matrix model, its planar expansion, eigenvalue saddle, and critical exponent. The formal combinatorial integral must be distinguished from a convergent integral over real Hermitian matrices. Record 695 revisits the counting conventions.

speaker: V. L. Ginzburg
title: Generalized Lie algebras: manuscript attribution to D. Gurevich
summary: The catalogue identifies Ginzburg on 29 September. The original heading on P001303 instead reads D. Gurevich, 13 October 1986, followed by generalized Lie algebras and groups. We retain the catalogue record but attribute the surviving mathematical items explicitly to D. I. Gurevich. They concern involutive Yang--Baxter operators, braided Lie identities, super and color examples, and braided commutators. Kazakov begins later on P001304.

speaker: V. A. Kazakov
title: Ising spins on random triangulations and Wick expansion
summary: The catalogue date is preserved, but this exposition begins after the Gurevich heading dated 13 October and occupies P001304--P001306. It introduces annealed Ising gravity, a two-matrix representation, a critical temperature, and a Wick-theorem intervention by A. N. Varchenko. Ginzburg\textquotesingle s braid discussion starts with the next dated heading and is not part of this record.

speaker: V. L. Ginzburg
title: Polynomial monodromy and the Burau representation
summary: The actual mathematical section is P001307--P001308. It constructs braid representations from cohomology of a punctured plane, identifies a Hecke relation, and asks faithfulness of Burau. The same letter is used for an exponent and a multiplicative monodromy parameter; the hyperelliptic example makes the ambiguity substantive.

speaker: A. A. Beilinson
title: The Deligne--Illusie proof of Hodge degeneration
summary: The short report at the top of P001309 announces an algebraic proof of degeneration of the Hodge--de Rham spectral sequence, referring to an Orsay preprint by Deligne and Illusie. The theorem over characteristic zero and the new positive-characteristic method are separate items.

speaker: V. A. Kazakov
title: Unitary orbital integrals and reduced gauge models
summary: The section from the lower part of P001309 through P001311 develops the Harish-Chandra--Itzykson--Zuber integral, recalls the principal-minor spherical-function formula, and explains the radial heat operator. It closes with a two-source integral and the Eguchi--Kawai matrix reduction. The final assertion that the reduced integral contains all gauge theory needs a center-symmetry qualification.

speaker: I. S. Zakharevich
title: Orbital integration, interlacing, and concentration remarks
summary: The new dated heading begins at P001312. The report revisits the orbital-integral heat proof and the spectral distribution of products of positive matrices, then uses sections of ellipsoids and interlacing arrays. Gelfand adds two high-dimensional intuition questions. Their printed numerical and dynamical assertions require separate qualifications.

speaker: B. V. Lidskii
title: The diagonal moment map
summary: The short intervention occupies the middle of P001313. It identifies the diagonal projection on a unitary orbit as a moment map and relates its Fourier transform to the orbital integral. The uncertain handwritten initial is not used to override the catalogue identification. Gelfand\textquotesingle s question about a super analogue of the symmetric group follows.

speaker: V. L. Ginzburg
title: Exact stationary phase and localization
summary: The lower part of P001313 gives an approximate Duistermaat--Heckman formula, its coadjoint-orbit example, and Gelfand\textquotesingle s questions about higher asymptotic terms and characteristic numbers. A final conjectural sentence is explicitly marked mine by the note-taker; it must not be attributed to Gelfand or Ginzburg.

speaker: G. I. Olshanskii
title: Spherical functions behind principal-minor integrals
summary: The actual exposition begins on P001314 and ends in the upper part of P001315. Olshanskii explains the Gelfand--Naimark formula through highest-weight characters and spherical functions, with HCIZ as a limiting form. Gelfand asks which other integrals admit such an interpretation.

speaker: V. G. Drinfeld
title: Quantizing KdV and the second Gelfand--Dickey bracket
summary: The section actually runs from the lower part of P001315 through P001318. It distinguishes the compatible KdV brackets, their free-field and Miura realizations, higher-order operators, and quantum commuting integrals. Gelfand and Feigin intervene. Three final questions concern quantization of KdV integrals, their spectrum in irreducible Virasoro representations, and general second-bracket quantization. The spectral question receives a bounded level-two development in this chapter; P001319 instead begins Beilinson on 10 November.

speaker: A. A. Beilinson
title: Virasoro uniformization and differential equations on moduli of curves
summary: The catalogue gives no page range, but the original P001319 heading clearly names Beilinson and 10 November 1986. The coherent continuation P001319--P001321 supplies surviving notes: formal-coordinate uniformization of pointed curves, determinant-line twists, and differential equations obtained from singular Virasoro vectors. This attribution is an explicit editorial recovery from the manuscript; the empty catalogue page field is retained. The note credits Kontsevich and Beilinson--Schechtman independently and refers to Belavin through Drinfeld.

speaker: V. A. Kazakov
title: Random surfaces, Gaussian embeddings, and coupled matrix integrals
summary: The actual section is P001322--P001325, jointly headed Kazakov and Zakharevich; interventions by Gelfand are marked. It compares the bosonic-string action with triangulated Gaussian surfaces, revisits weighted planar-map counting, and presents a two-source unitary integral and three-state matrix model. The final three- and four-dimensional gauge question repeats record 688. The lattice-theory report beginning P001326 belongs to record 696.

speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: Subspace configurations and preprojective reductions of modular lattices
summary: The manuscript section P001326--P001327 names a joint project with B. V. Lidskii and V. A. Ponomarev. It reviews subspace configurations and the free modular lattice, distinguishes word equality from linear equivalence, and announces a preprojective quotient and perfect elements. The printed 1987 paper supplies necessary restrictions omitted in the notebook. Finite axiomatizability, decidability, and classification of representations are different questions.

speaker: A. V. Zelevinsky
title: The unitary dual of general linear groups
summary: The talk begins on P001328 and ends at the top of P001330, before Kazakov. It reports the unitary-dual classification of Tadić and Vogan through determinant characters, complementary series, and normalized parabolic induction, then discusses square-integrable building blocks over local fields. Gelfand adds a kernel model for invariant Hermitian forms. The main formulas are recoverable, but the absolute-value normalization, modular character, center quotient, and segment exponents need correction or qualification.

speaker: V. A. Kazakov
title: Unitary integrals and the Ising model on random planar maps
summary: The identifiable talk begins on P001330. It moves from a unitary integral with several diagonal sources and reduced gauge models to the two-matrix representation of an Ising model on fluctuating planar maps. The ordinary Harish-Chandra--Itzykson--Zuber integral and biorthogonal-polynomial reduction are the calculational bridge. P001329 belongs to the preceding discussion; the February lecture starts on P001333.

title: YEAR 1987
summary: This is a catalogue heading marking the calendar-year transition, not a second mathematical lecture. The last Kazakov formulas occupy P001332; the next explicit manuscript date is 9 February 1987 on P001333. No independent mathematical occurrence is assigned to this structural record.

speaker: Don Zagier
title: Hecke traces, Eisenstein series, and the Riemann hypothesis
summary: After a question about polygon gluings, Zagier develops level-one modular forms, Hecke operators and a kernel proof of the Eichler--Selberg trace formula. The second half concerns Eisenstein series, horocycle averages and toroidal automorphic forms. Several normalizing constants in the notebook require correction. The talk ends at the dated heading on P001343; the wide catalogue interval overlaps both neighbours.

speaker: Don Zagier
title: Critical values and rational periods of modular forms
summary: The lecture connects even zeta-values, Eisenstein series and Mellin transforms of cusp forms, then explains the two rational period structures of Hecke eigenforms using Rankin unfolding. It explicitly points to Kohnen and Zagier\textquoteright s already published work on rational periods. The manuscript heading is on P001343 and the next lecture begins on P001349.

speaker: V. A. Kazakov
title: Gaussian matrix integrals and polygon gluings
summary: The talk gives the matrix-integral derivation of the Harer--Zagier enumeration of orientable polygon gluings, including Wick pairings, Hermitian eigenvalues, Hermite polynomials and generating functions. It closes with variants having triangular faces and colours. The identifiable text occupies P001349--P001354.

speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: Fractal measures, factors, and proposed connections
summary: The short Gelfand preamble on P001355 proposes connections among fractional-dimensional measures, representations, factors and chaotic dynamics. It includes a recognizable reference to the uniqueness of the hyperfinite type III\(_1\) factor, recorded with a problematic type label. The following explicit Beilinson heading controls attribution of the zeta-function material.

speaker: A. A. Beilinson
title: Zeta functions, regulators, and Artin L-functions
summary: Beilinson\textquoteright s explicit heading is on P001355 after Gelfand\textquoteright s factor discussion. His exposition continues through P001358, beyond the catalogue endpoint: archimedean and nonarchimedean local factors, special values, regulators, p-adic interpolation and Artin L-functions. The attribution follows the manuscript headings rather than the overlapping catalogue spans.

speaker: V. E. Zakharov
title: Dressing methods and spectral differential operators
summary: Zakharov reviews the Marchenko and nonlocal d-bar dressing constructions and then considers commuting operators that differentiate in the spectral parameter. The novelty claim concerns this last extension, not inverse scattering itself. Several displayed Lax and matrix identities have sign or hypothesis problems. The Migdal heading appears partway down P001363.

speaker: A. A. Migdal
title: Matrix loop equations and Wilson loops
summary: Migdal derives Schwinger--Dyson identities for matrix traces, planar factorization and the resolvent equation, before connecting them with gauge-theory loop equations. Gelfand interrupts with the cube-plane problem and its answer 96. The next dated meeting begins on P001368; P001362 and the beginning of P001363 remain Zakharov\textquoteright s.

speaker: Ya. G. Sinai
title: Spin glasses and ultrametricity
summary: Sinai\textquoteright s discussion on P001368--P001369 distinguishes finite-range spin glasses from the mean-field model, raises the thermodynamic ground-state problem, and describes the Parisi picture of hierarchical overlaps. Later theorems settle carefully specified mean-field assertions, but do not justify the literal finite-size statement of many exactly degenerate ground states.

speaker: A. S. Schwarz
title: Super Riemann surfaces and string measures
summary: The Schwarz heading occurs on P001369 after Sinai\textquoteright s discussion and continues into P001371. The talk treats superconformal distributions, moduli, periods, super Selberg formulas and determinants in string theory. Statements about uniformization, free modules and determinant powers need qualifications; the catalogue record number, date and interval are retained, with the manuscript order identified explicitly.

speaker: D. V. Alekseevskii
title: Quaternionic structures and integrability
summary: The Alekseevskii heading on P001371 introduces the failure of a naive quaternionic differentiability condition, quaternionic projective changes of coordinates, and the invariant rank-three bundle of almost complex structures. The discussion distinguishes torsion-free quaternionic geometry from a chosen hypercomplex triple and includes a twistor-style integrability proposal.

speaker: A. A. Kirillov
title: Hecke algebras, braids, and link invariants
summary: After Gelfand\textquoteright s incompletely specified question about commuting partially defined isometries, Kirillov explains Hecke algebras, braid groups and Markov traces. The notes conflate algebraic traces, positive traces and factor representations, and the observation about roots of unity should be read against Jones\textquoteright s pre-existing index theorem.

speaker: A. A. Beilinson
title: Holomorphic Chern classes and their integral comparison
summary: The explicit Beilinson heading on P001376 starts with Chern classes and their Hodge and integral structures, then formulates the comparison problem using transition functions and logarithms. This is the introduction to the following week\textquoteright s Deligne-cohomology lecture, not a second copy of that lecture.

speaker: A. A. Beilinson
title: Deligne cohomology, motivic complexes, and the dilogarithm
summary: The lecture defines the Deligne complex, its products and characteristic classes, explains the intermediate-Jacobian exact sequence, and sketches motivic refinements and the weight-two dilogarithmic complex. It cites the MPI 87-2 preprint explicitly. The last cross-ratio construction is best matched to the low-weight motivic characteristic-class program; its abbreviation is not a proof of the general motivic conjectures.
